title: Purification and cryo-EM structure determination of Arabidopsis thaliana GLR3.4
protocol: Thaw DH10Bac competent cells on ice.
Dispense 25–30 μL of DH10Bac competent cells into a prechilled 1.5-mL polypropylene tube.
Add approximately 1–10 ng (1–2 μL) of plasmid DNA to the tube and mix gently by flicking/tapping several times.
Incubate on ice for 15–30 min.
Transfer the tube to a water bath at 42°C for 45 s.
Immediately transfer the tube back to ice after heat shock and let it cool on ice for 2–3 min.
Add 200 μL SOC media to the tube.
Transfer the tube to an incubator shaker set at 220 rpm.
Incubate for 4 h at 37°C.
Pipette 20–100 μL of transformation reaction onto plates.
Spread the reaction evenly on the plates.
Incubate the plates for at least 24 h at 37°C.
Carefully inoculate a single white colony in 5–6 mL LB broth supplemented with appropriate antibiotics.
Incubate for 12–15 h at 37°C with continuous rotation at 220–250 rpm.
Centrifuge the culture at ∼3,100 g for 10 min.
Decant to discard the supernatant and save the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL resuspension buffer until homogeneous via pipetting up and down or by vortexing.
Transfer the suspension to a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 200 μL lysis buffer and mix by gently inverting the tube several (∼15–20) times.
Add 200 μL neutralization buffer and mix by gentle inversion several (∼20) times.
Centrifuge the tube at ∼21,100 g for 10 min at ∼20°C–25°C.
Avoiding the pellet, carefully collect and transfer the supernatant to a fresh 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
In the fume hood, add an equal volume of Tris equilibrated Phenol:Chloroform: Isoamyl-alcohol (25:24:1) and mix by inverting gently several times for 1 min.
Spin at ∼21,100 g for 5 min at ∼20°C–25°C.
In the fume hood, gently collect the top layer supernatant and transfer it to a new 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 2× volume of ice-cold 100% ethanol, mix well by gently inverting for 30 s, and incubate at −20°C for a minimum of 30 min.
Centrifuge at ∼21,100 g for 20–30 min at 4°C.
Carefully decant to discard the supernatant and add 1 mL ice-cooled 70% ethanol.
Invert the tube gently several times to wash the pellet.
Centrifuge for 5 min at ∼21,100 g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant by gentle aspiration.
To avoid traces of remaining ethanol, air dry the pellet for 15–20 min at ∼20°C–25°C in a fume hood.
Add 40–50 μL of autoclaved milli-Q water and dissolve the pellet by gentle tapping/flicking.
Place the tube with bacmid DNA on ice.
Store the bacmid DNA at −80°C for an extended period.
Work under sterile conditions in a laminar hood.
Add 2 mL of Sf9 cells per well in a 6-well plate with a density of 0.5–0.75 ×10^6/mL (1–1.5 ×10^6 cells per P1 virus).
Allow the cells to adhere for 30 min to 1 h in a dark incubator at 27°C.
In an Eppendorf tube, add 180 μL of SF900 media, 10 μL of Cellfectin II, and 10 μL of thawed bacmid DNA.
Tap the tube to mix.
Let the mixture sit for 20–30 min in the hood.
Add the mixture dropwise to the cells in the well.
Incubate the plate at 27°C for 4–6 days.
Monitor cell behavior and fluorescence under a microscope if the gene of interest is fused with a fluorescent marker gene.
Harvest the P1 virus by filtering 2 mL medium using a 0.2 μm sterile syringe filter in a laminar hood.
Store the filtered virus at 4°C protected from light for up to 4–6 months.
Infect 500 mL of Sf9 cells at a cell density of 1.5×10^6 cells/mL in a 1-L non-baffled Erlenmeyer flask by adding 500 μL of P1 virus under sterile conditions in a laminar hood.
Incubate the Sf9 cell culture in a shaker at 27°C and 115 rpm for 72–120 hours, protected from light.
Centrifuge the culture at ∼5,000 g for 15 minutes at 4°C in a Sorvall centrifuge.
Discard the cell pellet and save the supernatant containing the P2 virus.
Ultracentrifuge the supernatant at 4°C for 1 hour at ∼61,000 g in a preparative ultracentrifuge with a Type 45Ti Beckman Coulter rotor.

Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 50 or 25 mL Gibco FreeStyle 293 expression media supplemented with 2% of γ-irradiated fetal bovine serum (FBS) to get 10× or 20× concentrated P2 virus, respectively.
Pass the resuspension through a 0.22 μm filter into a sterile 50-mL tube and store at 4°C well protected from light.

In a laminar hood and sterile conditions, prepare 800 mL of HEK 293S GnTI− cell culture at the density of 2.5–3.5 × 106 cells/mL maintained in Freestyle 293 media supplemented with 2% FBS in a 2-L baffled Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 8 mL of 20× concentrated P2 virus stock to the cell culture.
Incubate the cell culture at 37°C in an orbital shaker at 110 rpm and 5% CO2.
Add 10 mM of sodium butyrate to the culture 12–20 h post-transduction.
Decrease the incubator temperature to 30°C.
After 72–74 h post-transduction, harvest the cells by centrifugation at ∼5,000 g for 15 min at 4°C in a Sorvall RC 5B Plus centrifuge.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cell pellet by resuspension in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 8.0).
Transfer the suspension to a 50-mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at ∼3,100 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and store the cell pellet at -80°C until further use.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ice-cold Cell Lysis buffer.
Add a stir bar and ∼40 mL of the Cell Lysis buffer to the 50-mL falcon tube with the frozen cell pellet until it reaches 45-mL volume.
Resuspend the pellet by rocking on a platform or by vortexing until the cell pellet becomes detached and dissolved.
Disrupt the cells by sonication using Misonix Sonicator with a preset program of six cycles (3 min total process time) at amplitude 8, 15 s pulse on time, and 15 s pulse off time.
Repeat the sonication process 2 more times or until optimal cell lysis.
Centrifuge the cell lysate suspension at ∼3,100 g for 10 min at 4°C to remove cell debris and unbroken cells.
Collect the clarified supernatant by decanting into a prechilled polycarbonate bottle assembly for ultracentrifugation.
Ultracentrifuge in a Type 45Ti Beckman Coulter fixed-angle rotor at ∼186,000 g for 1 hour at 4°C to obtain the membrane fraction.

Discard the supernatant and mechanically homogenize the obtained membrane fraction pellet using a prechilled dounce homogenizer with plunger moved forth and back at least 6 times in Cell Lysis buffer (∼25 mL).

Solubilize the membrane protein from the homogenate by adding an equal volume of solubilization buffer containing digitonin to the homogenate (totaling ∼50 mL), stir/rotate at low-medium speed for ∼2 hours at 4°C.
Ultracentrifuge the solubilizate at ∼186,000 g in a Type 45Ti Beckman Coulter fixed-angle rotor at 4°C for 1 hour to remove insoluble material.
Collect the supernatant and add 2 mL of strep resin prewashed and equilibrated in T buffer.
Rotate the mix for 12–14 hours at 4°C.
Equilibrate a 30-mL chromatography gravity column by rinsing with milli-Q water and allowing SEC buffer to flow through.
Transfer the AtGLR3.4 protein-bound strep resin to the empty pre-equilibrated gravity chromatography column and collect the flow-through.
Wash the resin by pouring 25 mL of SEC buffer into the column.
Elute the AtGLR3.4 protein with ∼10–15 mL of freshly made Strep Elution buffer.
Observe the eGFP-tagged protein eluting from the column by the color change to green and the resin becoming white.
Measure the concentration of the protein using a spectrophotometer set to A280 (absorbance at 280 nm) blanked with the elution buffer.
Add 1/300 (w/w) thrombin to the protein solution and incubate at 22°C for 90 min to cleave off eGFP and the strep tag.
Concentrate the thrombin digest reaction to ∼500 μL using a 100-kDa NMWL centrifugal filter.
Transfer the concentrated protein to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Centrifuge the concentrated protein at ∼86,500 g for 30 min at 4°C using a Sorvall MTX150 Micro-Ultracentrifuge and a S100AT4 rotor.
Avoid the pellet and inject the supernatant into a 500-μL loop connected to a Superose™ 6 10/300 GL SEC column attached to an AKTA FPLC (GE Healthcare) pre-equilibrated in SEC Buffer.
Run the SEC column at 0.5 mL/min and pool peak fractions corresponding to AtGLR3.4 tetramer.
Concentrate pooled fractions to 3–4 mg/mL using a 100-kDa NMWL centrifugal filter.
Store concentrated, purified protein at 4°C for up to one week.
Inspect the purity of the protein by sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE).
Deposit approximately 50 nm of gold onto the grids using an Edwards Auto 306 evaporator.
Remove carbon from the grid with the Gatan Solarus (model 950) Advanced Plasma Cleaning System Ar/O2 treatment for 4 minutes at 50 watts, with 35.0 sccm Argon and 11.5 sccm Oxygen.
Subject grids to a H2/O2 plasma treatment using the Gatan Solarus (model 950) Advanced Plasma Cleaning System (20 seconds at 10 watts, with 6.4 sccm H2 and 27.5 sccm O2).
Ultracentrifuge purified protein sample at approximately 86,500 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant to a prechilled tube, avoiding any possible protein precipitation.
Set the vitrobot to 4°C with 100% humidity.
Wait for 15 seconds before blotting.
Blot for 4–5 seconds with a force of 4–5.
Apply 3 μL of purified AtGLR3.4 protein at 3–3.5 mg/mL to the gold-coated side of the grid.
Plunge freeze the grid into liquid ethane cooled to approximately −190°C in liquid nitrogen using a Mark IV vitrobot.
Test grids on screening transmission electron microscopes (TEMs) such as Glacios or F20 (FEI Thermo Scientific).
Assess particle distribution, orientation, and ice quality during testing.
Collect cryo-EM data from prescreened grids on a FEI Titan Krios TEM operating at 300 kV.
Use a direct electron detection (DED) camera in counting mode with approximately 50 frames per movie.
Maintain a total dose of approximately 58 electrons per Å² during data collection.
Set the physical pixel size to approximately 0.83 Å.
Adjust the defocus value between −0.5 and −2.5 μm for optimal results.
Process the data in RELION 3.1.
Perform beam-induced motion correction using MotionCor2 with a dose per frame of 1.16, EER fractionation -32, B Factor -150, and number of patches 5×5.
Estimate contrast transfer function (CTF) using CTFFIND4.1 in RELION 3.1.
Manually pick approximately 3,000 particles by selecting any particle shape that commonly appears in the micrographs.
2D-classify these manually selected particles to generate templates for further template-based auto picking in RELION 3.1.
Bin picked particle images 4×4 to a pixel size of approximately 3.32 Å/pixel.
Subject binned particle images to 3D classification into 10 classes with C1 symmetry.
Select the best classes that correspond to the Y shape of iGluR.
Vary the regularization parameter (T) and iterations for 3D classification.
Use T=4 and iterations = 40 in 3D classification without angular sampling.
Perform multiple rounds of 3D classification into 8 classes.
Refine particles from the best class using C2 symmetry.
Postprocess to yield a map with resolution of 3.73Å from 118,592 particles (FSC=0.143) in RELION.
Import particles from the last 3D refinement job into cryoSPARC.
Clean up particles by 2D classification in cryoSPARC.
Select best 2D classes and subject corresponding particles to homogeneous and non-uniform refinement applying C2 symmetry.
Achieve a map with resolution of 3.57 Å (FSC = 0.143) from 110,630 particles after non-uniform refinement in cryoSPARC.
Estimate local resolution using unfiltered half-maps and Resmap.
Use UCSF Chimera to visualize the EM density maps.
Build atomic models of AtGLR3.4 once high-resolution cryo-EM map is obtained.
Use the crystal structure of AtGLR3.4-S1S2 (PDB: 7LZ0) to build the ligand-binding domain.
Perform homology modeling in SWISS-MODEL using the GluA2 crystal structure (PDB: 3KG2) as a guide to build the amino terminal and transmembrane domains.
Finalize model building manually using COOT.
Build two subunits, A and B, for AtGLR3.4.
Duplicate the AB dimer following the C2 symmetry of the map to make the CD dimer.
Assemble the ABCD tetramer from the duplicated dimers.
Refine the obtained atomic model of AtGLR3.4 in real-space using PHENIX.
Validate the model quality using MolProbity (score = 1.69, clash score = 4.49, poor rotamers = 0.44%).
Evaluate EMRinger (EMRinger score = 2.41, optimal Threshold = 0.67, Rotamer-ratio = 0.77) in Phenix for model validation.
